opportunity: A call's TRAILING register argument can be a value a previous call's clobber left behind: Heritage::guard_calls plants an INDIRECT creation for a killed-by-call register that is also a possible OUTPUT location of the callee's model (rdx on x86-64, because a 16-byte value returns in rax:rdx), AncestorRealistic::enter_node answers realistic for it and records ind_create_formed, and fillin_map_standard marks every active trial used. Upstream reads that bit back on the RETURN list only (fillin_map_standard_out), so the evidence that disqualifies a return value is ignored for an argument. coreutils fmt -O2 main renders sub_3700(stdin,"-",v10) against a DWARF prototype of two parameters, with two `// rdx` locals that are never assigned.
test_name: tests/stages/kuna-argclobber.xml (4 two-pass assertions on a hand-assembled x86-64 bytechunk: a call clobber on one path of the argument register's join and a dead idivl remainder on the other) + tests/stages/kuna-argclobber-guards.xml (the callee-reads clause, same caller shape) + tests/stages/kuna-argclobber-armreturn.xml (the same-register clause, ARM, the u-boot repro reduced) + tests/stages/kuna-argclobber-forward.xml (the join clause: the caller forwards its own second parameter on the non-clobber path, so both the argument and the parameter survive both passes)
inspiration: upstream ParamListStandardOut::fillinMap (fspec.cc:1721) applied to the input list; witness coreutils fmt -O2 main 0x26a0 -> fmt 0x3700 at 0x2ac1
root_cause: Not a kuna scheduling divergence and not the is_checked() guard. Instrumented (KUNA_DBG_TRIAL) on the witness call: the RDX trial is checked on ActionActiveParam pass 0, the three-input MULTIEQUAL already exists at that point, AncestorRealistic returns realistic=1 solid=0 and sets ind_create_formed=1, and the trial is active+used from then on. The bit IS set (contradicting the refuter's inference, which mis-anchored fspec.rs:3249/:3264-3267 to fillin_map_standard; those lines are inside fillin_map_standard_out, fn at :3235). The input list simply has no reader of the bit, faithfully to upstream: stock Ghidra emits the same three-argument call on the same binary and names the phantoms extraout_RDX/extraout_RDX_00.

witness.before: v12 = sub_3700(stdin,"-",v10);  /  v3 = sub_3700(stdin,v6);  /  v12 &= sub_3700(v5);   (3/2/1 arguments, `unsigned long v9; // rdx` and `unsigned long v11; // rdx` never assigned)
witness.after: v9 = sub_3700(stdin,"-");  /  v3 = sub_3700(stdin,v6);  /  v9 &= sub_3700(v5,v6);   (2/2/2, DWARF says fmt(FILE *, char const *))

corpus_sweep.method: kuna decompile-all, whole binary, option off vs on, per-function diff with vN renumbering normalized; every changed call group then classified against the callee's OWN recovered prototype arity and, where one exists, against DWARF or the library's own header. Artifact: docs/features/phantomargs/sweep-2026-09-16.txt
corpus_sweep.shape: every changed site loses exactly one TRAILING argument, 3->2, and all four are ONE shape: the argument register's join has a call clobber on one path and a dead idiv remainder on the other. No call site appears or disappears and no statement moves. No control-flow change in the swept set; the only brace-level change is an e2fsck `if` whose block went from two statements to one.
corpus_sweep.ground_truth: all four sites land on the arity of the callee's own recovered prototype (2 in every case), and all four callees also have an external prototype that agrees: fmt(FILE *f, char const *file) has exactly 2 DW_TAG_formal_parameter on the unstripped decbench twin (both the -O2 and the -O2-noinline build); ext2fs_dblist_sort2(dblist, sortfunc) is 2 in the e2fsprogs public header; xrealloc(void *, size_t) is 2 in bash's xmalloc.h.
corpus_sweep.control_flow_changes: 0 in the swept set (46 binaries / 41,258 functions)
corpus_sweep.false_positive_avoided: tar parse_datetime2 @0x48e10 -> str_days @0x46550 (DWARF: 3 params). Its RDX trial is MULTIEQUAL(COPY, MULTIEQUAL) -- the clobber is one phi deeper -- so the direct-clobber clause declines it and the real argument is kept.
corpus_sweep.option_off_is_inert: kuna decompile-all with the option OFF is byte-identical to the pinned pre-change binary on all four binaries the option changes plus four controls (fmt, e2fsck, bash, grep, u-boot, ssh-keygen, crazyflie cf2.elf, betaflight): 0 differing lines each.

ground_truth_check.method: readelf --debug-dump=info on the unstripped decbench twin (DW_TAG_formal_parameter count at the callee's DW_AT_low_pc), or the project's own public header for a named import
ground_truth_check.fmt 0x3700: fmt(FILE *f, char const *file), 2 DW_TAG_formal_parameter (kuna rendered 3 at one site)
ground_truth_check.fmt -O2-noinline 0x3a30: the same function in the -O2-noinline build, same DWARF
ground_truth_check.e2fsck ext2fs_dblist_sort2: 2 parameters (ext2_dblist, EXT2_QSORT_TYPE (*)(...)) in the e2fsprogs public header
ground_truth_check.tar 0x46550: str_days, 3 params -- declined by the direct-clobber clause

benchmark.method: kuna decompile-all --addr <fn> --json, variables[] rows (kind, name-class, type) compared off vs on, on ALL 4 functions the sweep changes, with the automatic vN names normalized. The pass can in principle delete a `kind: arg` row, so this is measured rather than argued.

changed_rows.bash 0xe30d0 (expand_prompt): one row changes: the uncommitted `undefined8` framelayout slot local_a0 becomes a typed `char *` stack variable. That is a type_match gain, not a loss. Row count is unchanged at 32.

speed.method: interleaved off/on pairs, MINIMUM of 21 pairs, `kuna decompile-all <bin> --addr <fn> --option argclobber off|on` (the CLI surface that rejects a bad option value). Re-measured after the review clauses landed; the box was running the workspace suite throughout, so these are pessimistic.
speed.why: with the option off the first statement returns on a bool. With it on the added work is two reads of an already-built summary: the same-register test walks one join's inputs, and the callee test is a lookup in the per-image CalleeEntryDead map calleedeadarg (default on) already populates. The control binary's +0.40% is the measurement floor on a loaded box.

clauses: the clobber reaches the call directly: the defining op is the indirect creation, or a MULTIEQUAL one of whose immediate inputs is one

every one of those indirect creations is a creation of THE ARGUMENT REGISTER ITSELF (added in review round 2; the first return register of every ABI is also killed-by-call and a possible output location, so a preceding call's result is an indirect creation too)

EVERY OTHER INPUT OF THAT JOIN is a division by-product -- what an idiv leaves in the remainder register while the caller uses only the quotient (added in review round 3; without it one clobber input condemned the whole join and a value the caller demonstrably wrote on another path, including the caller's own parameter, was deleted with it)
the callee's own body does not read those register bytes before writing them (CalleeEntryDead::proves_input; added in review round 2)
trailing: no used trial follows it
at least one used argument remains
no already-final sibling call to the same callee entry in this function passed an argument in that storage

ablation: MEASURED, not asserted: with the default flipped to `true` in Architecture and ArchContext and the tree rebuilt, `kuna test --datatests --baseline docs/baseline.json` is 675/675 PARITY OK and `--datatests-dir tests/stages --baseline docs/baseline-stages.json` is 1021/1021 PARITY OK. The flip was reverted; the shipped default is off, and it is off because of the rax:rdx return shape no clause can see and because a wrong drop is a DELETED expression, not because of the corpora.

review_round3.blocker: clobber_of_this_register_reaches put no condition on a MULTIEQUAL input whose def was not an indirect creation, so one clobber among a join's incoming values condemned the whole join. Repro (20-line .s, gcc -nostdlib -static, no corpus binary needed): a caller that forwards its own second parameter into rdx on the non-clobber path rendered `void sub_401000(long a0)` / `sub_40102f(a0,5)` with the option on, against `void sub_401000(long a0,unsigned long a1)` / `sub_40102f(a0,5,a1)` off -- both the argument and the parameter deleted, including from the scored variables[] surface.
review_round3.close: the join clause (clause 4). Both reviewer repros (fix.s, the constant; fix2.s, the forwarded parameter) now render identically with the option on and off, and the fmt witness still collapses 3/2/1 -> 2/2/2.
review_round3.yield_after_tightening: the sweep fell from 45 changed functions over 33 binaries to 4 over 46. The classes that went away -- openssh (30 of round 2's 47 call groups), betaflight (5), u-boot (2), dpkg (2), grep (1) -- all had a value the caller wrote on some path of the join; ssh-keygen 0x9b20 is the representative, where the non-clobber input is `"PIN incorrect"` loaded for a different call. The round-2 note that a liveness proxy 'cost 55 of 57 correct drops' had the framing backwards: those drops had no caller-side evidence.
